title: The emerging role: context curator architect
oneliner: LLMs can write the code, but someone must design what the model is allowed to see - guardrails, memory schemas, data boundaries. That someone is the context curator.
says: Since LLMs can now write and execute code, software engineers may fear for their jobs. His counter: your understanding of systems remains critically important. The emerging role is the context curator architect - the person who thinks in terms of system guardrails, memory schemas, and where data boundaries should be defined, then prepares those clearly as tasks for the LLM to execute.
explained: The insight underneath: an LLM's output quality is bounded by its input context. A model handed a vague task produces generic code; a model handed precise guardrails, a well-designed memory of the system, and clear data boundaries produces work that fits. Designing that context is architecture - it requires knowing the system's real constraints, which is exactly what models lack.

So the engineer's value migrates up a level: from writing syntax to specifying the world the syntax must live in. This is not a consolation prize; it is the same shift his platform series makes at the org level. Season 2's prompt registry and RAG-as-a-service are context curation as shared platform services - the role, industrialized.
takeaway: Stop competing with the model on syntax; own what it cannot - system constraints, memory design, and data boundaries. Context design is the durable skill.
